entities.name: National University of Colombia
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The National University of Colombia (Universidad Nacional de Colombia, UNAL), founded in 1867 during the Liberal Olympus period of Colombian political history — when secular liberal reformers sought to modernize Colombian education against conservative Catholic educational hegemony — is Colombia's largest and most prestigious public university, with approximately 50,000 students across 9 campuses in Bogotá, Medellín, Manizales, Palmira, and other cities, and consistently ranked as Latin America's top 20 universities.

UNAL's founding in 1867 under President Santos Acosta was an explicitly liberal act: the university was established as a secular, state-controlled institution to train engineers, agronomists, lawyers, and scientists outside Church influence — a project of Colombian modernity that paralleled similar liberal university reforms across Latin America (including Córdoba's 1918 University Reform, see below). The institution was central to training the technical and professional classes that built Colombia's republican institutions.

Through Colombia's complex 20th-century history — including the La Violencia period (1948-1958, approximately 200,000 killed), FARC guerrilla conflict (1964-2016), and narco-trafficking crises — UNAL has been both a site of political mobilization and a refuge for intellectual life. The university's Bogotá campus is famous for political activism; student movements have historically engaged with every major Colombian political crisis. Today UNAL combines strong programs in engineering, natural sciences, agriculture, medicine, and the humanities with a public university mission serving Colombia's diverse national population through accessible low-cost education.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The National University of Colombia — founded in 1867 as a secular liberal institution against Catholic educational dominance, training Colombia's professional class through 155 years of conflict and political crisis, and maintaining the country's premier research university mission — is central to Colombian intellectual and national development history.
